one_liner: Multi-threaded, AVX-vectorized out-of-place tensor transposition (B = alpha*perm(A) + beta*B); paper reports large wins over Eigen's tensor shuffle.
what_it_does: HPTT computes an arbitrary-rank permutation of a dense tensor into a separate output buffer, optionally scaling the input (alpha) and accumulating into the output (beta), for float, double and their complex types, in column- or row-major layout, and on sub-tensors through outerSize arguments. The API is FFTW-like: hptt::create_plan(perm, dim, alpha, A, sizeA, outerSizeA, beta, B, outerSizeB, method, numThreads) returns a shared_ptr plan that you execute() and can re-point at new buffers with setInputPtr/setOutputPtr. A one-shot C interface (sTensorTranspose, dTensorTranspose, cTensorTranspose, zTensorTranspose) and a ctypes Python module (hptt.transpose, ascontiguousarray, asfortranarray) wrap the same engine. It is not a drop-in for Eigen's shuffle() or numpy.transpose: you pass raw pointers and index arrays.
how_it_is_fast: Size-1 indices are dropped and indices that stay adjacent under the permutation are fused, which lowers the effective rank. The remaining loop nest is cut into blocks that a register-level micro-kernel transposes in-register (8x8 for float and 4x4 for double with AVX unpack/shuffle, 4x4 float on NEON), with software prefetch of the next A and B blocks and non-temporal streaming stores (_mm256_stream_ps/pd) when beta is 0 and B is 32-byte aligned, which avoids write-allocate traffic. A cost model picks a loop order and an OpenMP parallelization strategy (prime-factor split of the loops for load balance); hptt::MEASURE, PATIENT and CRAZY instead time candidate plans for up to 10 s, 60 s or 1 h, FFTW-style.
when_to_use: You need a materialized permuted copy of a rank-3 to rank-6 dense tensor (for example before a GEMM in a TTGT tensor contraction, or for layout conversion between libraries) and the copy is memory-bandwidth-bound
Repeated transpositions of the same shape and permutation: build the plan once (optionally autotuned with MEASURE) and reuse it with setInputPtr/setOutputPtr
Multi-core x86 machines with AVX, where the paper reports bandwidth close to SAXPY and the README figure shows 5x to 20x over numpy.transpose(...).copy() with 24 threads
Fused scale-and-accumulate transposes (B = alpha*perm(A) + beta*B), including complex conjugation through setConjA, which Eigen's shuffle() and numpy need extra passes for
Python code that copies large non-contiguous numpy views (np.ascontiguousarray after a transpose) and can tolerate a ctypes wrapper that needs HPTT_ROOT and psutil
when_not_to_use: In-place transposition, or plain 2-D matrix transposes where an in-place or BLAS-extension routine (mkl_simatcopy, the transpose-scale sibling) avoids the second buffer: HPTT is out-of-place only

AArch64 or Apple Silicon: the NEON kernel's partial specialization in src/transpose.cpp (around line 247) names micro_kernel<float, betaIsZero> without the conjA argument, and the build files pass the ARMv7-only -mfpu=neon; open PR #35 fixes both, and also turns off GCC auto-vectorization of transpose_int on Apple Silicon. The paper's ARM results are ARMv7

MSVC or strict ISO C++ builds: the code uses variable-length arrays, __restrict__, GCC attributes and float _Complex in C++ (open issue #26; Clang 13 also rejects the _Complex casts in src/hptt.cpp, issue #21)
Libraries that must not terminate the host process: invalid sizes, permutations or outer sizes print to stderr and call exit(-1), not throw (issue #17, open since 2019)

Sub-tensor transposes with outerSize > size where an innermost dimension is 1: open PR #33 reports that transpose_int then picks the wrong innermost index; check results for that shape class or apply the PR

integration.dependencies: OpenMP (optional in the code, but the build files add -fopenmp/-qopenmp only for compilers they recognize); Python interface needs numpy and psutil
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 with GNU extensions (VLAs, __restrict__, float _Complex); README says tested with icpc 15-17, g++ 5.4-6.3 and clang++ 3.8/3.9; CMake 3.7+. Makefile also builds libhptt.so
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX (make avx / -DENABLE_AVX=ON; no AVX2 or AVX-512 kernels), ARMv7 NEON (AArch64 needs PR #35), scalar fallback elsewhere; IBM POWER kernel is commented out
integration.thread_safety: not documented for concurrent execute() on one plan (a plan holds mutable A/B pointers, alpha and beta); addThreadId() is lock-protected, and execute_expert<..., spawnThreads=false, ...>() is meant to be called from inside an existing OpenMP parallel region with explicit thread ids
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the Python module offers hptt.transpose/ascontiguousarray/asfortranarray as numpy-like calls, but hptt.transpose returns a materialized copy rather than a view, and issue #30 reports ascontiguousarray raising 'repeated axis in transpose' where numpy does not; there is no Eigen-compatible API

gotchas: Autotuning (MEASURE/PATIENT/CRAZY) runs candidate plans on your real A and B during create_plan; the header says the data is restored afterwards unless A holds NaN or inf

execute() always requests streaming stores; they are used when beta is 0 and B is suitably aligned, which pushes B out of cache. If you read B right away (small tensors, packing for GEMM), call execute_expert<false, ...>() as the header advises

CMake attaches -fopenmp -march=native -mtune=native as PUBLIC compile options, so they propagate to targets that link hptt and make the binary host-specific; the Makefile adds OpenMP only when CXX is exactly icpc, g++ or clang++, so CXX=/usr/bin/g++ or g++-13 silently builds a single-threaded library (issue #36)

verifyParameter writes found[perm[i]] before checking that perm[i] is in range, and the row-major conversion runs before it, so an out-of-range permutation entry is an out-of-bounds access rather than a clean error; per-dimension sizes are int
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick HPTT when you need the permuted tensor itself (any rank, out-of-place, with alpha/beta); transpose-scale (hpit) covers in-place 2-D transpose with scaling against mkl_simatcopy, and TBLIS avoids explicit transposition altogether when the end goal is a contraction. TCCG builds on HPTT for its TTGT path, so HPTT is the piece to take if you only need the transposition.
verified_claims_summary: The headline is from the peer-reviewed ARRAY 2017 paper, seen only through search-result abstracts: bandwidth comparable to SAXPY across Ivy Bridge, ARMv7 and Power7, 'remarkable speedups' over Eigen's tensor transposition (up to 27.4x per the verifier's search quote; the snippet seen here gave no number), and up to 3.1x faster CTF contractions; the CPU, compiler and thread counts behind the Eigen figure were not visible. The repo's own figure compares HPTT with 24 threads on 2x Xeon E5-2680 v3 against numpy.transpose(...).copy() (thread count and compiler not stated; numpy's copy is normally single-threaded) over 57 cases, about 5.1x to 19.7x read by eye, so much of that gap is parallel bandwidth; the C++ benchmark harness compares only with a naive reference and the original TTC.
status_note: Unmaintained: last commit 2022-02-15, with 15 open issues and 7 open PRs (including the AArch64 fix #35 and the sub-tensor correctness fix #33) and no maintainer replies; BSD-3-Clause and only four source files, so it is easy to vendor with those patches applied.
